1.

The present claim petition is based on Detailed Accident Report (Dar) filed under section
159/166 clause (4) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (herein after Act) by the investigating officer of Fir
No. 351/19 Police Station Kalyanpuri, Delhi.

1

2.
The accident in the present case took place on 26.07.2019.

It is the case of the petitioner that at around 06:30 A.M., he was going on foot towards Jalebi Chowk via road between 09-10 Block,
Khichripur, Delhi.

When he reached just before the main road, suddenly a motorcycle bearing Registration No. DL-4SCF-6004 came from the side of main road being driven in a zig-zag manner by its driver i.e. Respondent No.1. R1 came driving in a rash, reckless and negligent manner and on a high speed and hit him.
As a result of forceful hit, he fell down on the road and received grievous injuries.
No audio-visual signal was given by the driver of the motorcycle before the accident.
After the accident, petitioner was removed to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, Khichripur where MLC was prepared and treatment was given to him.
He was referred to higher centre and he was admitted in MAX Healthcare Hospital, Patparganj, Delhi on 27.07.2019.
There, he was treated and splint was applied on his left lower leg and plan for ORIF (Open reduction and internal fixation) was made.
He was discharged from the hospital on 28.07.2019 due to non-availability of bed, with advice to follow-up the treatment given in hospital and he was referred to some other higher centre.
Thereafter, he was treated in Shanti Mukund Hospital.
His treatment continued for about 04 months.
3. All of the respondents put in their appearance but R1 & R2 failed to file written statement and their opportunity to file written statement stood closed vide order dt. 09.02.2021.
R3 and R4 filed Written Statements on their behalf.
3(i). Separate Written Statement has been filed on behalf of Respondent No. 3.
It is stated that he had bought the vehicle in year 2014.
It is further submitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured at the time of accident.
It is stated that R3 was running a business of electrical items in the name and style of H2O Engineers and Solutions and has various employees.
One of the employees namely Lalit/R2, who was holding a valid driving licence, was allowed to drive the vehicle for official purpose.
The use of motorcycle by R1, if any, was without authorization from R3 and, therefore, R3 is liable.
R2 had authority to drive the offending vehicle only for office/work purpose and he holds a valid driving licence.
R1 is not known to R3 and R3 has no personal knowledge that the alleged offending vehicle was given to R1 by R2.

It is stated further that IO has alleged involvement of offending vehicle on the basis of purported CCTV Footage but the same is not filed on record and that the copy of FIR and statement of witnesses is not legible.
It is further stated that no photograph of spot is filed by IO and site plan is incomplete.

4. Respondent No.4/United India Insurance Company Ltd. has mentioned in its written statement that the vehicle bearing No. DL- 4SCF-6004 was being driven by R1 without valid and effective driving licence.
Hence, insurance company is not liable to indemnify the insured/R3.
IO has supplied incomplete and illegible documents.
IO has not filed any photograph and site plan is incomplete.
No CCTV Footage is filed by IO despite the claim of involvement of alleged offending vehicle on the basis of purported CCTV footage obtained from nearby shop.
Offending vehicle was insured from 18.01.2019 to 17.01.2020.
Other general defences have been taken by R4/Insurer.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed on 08.06.2022:-
Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
2 (i) Whether the petitioner Vijender @ Bijender Pal suffered grievous injuries in a motor vehicular accident which took place on 26.07.2019 at 11:00 P.M., near Block 9 & 10, Khichripur Road, Khichripur, Delhi, within the jurisdiction of PS Kalyanpuri,
due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle bearing Registration No.
DL-4SCF-6004 being driven by Respondent No.1/Manish?

(OPP) 
(ii) Whether there was breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy as Respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident?
(OPR-3)
(iii) Whether petitioner is entitled to compensation , on account of said injuries and if yes, to what extent and from whom?

(OPP) 
(iv) Relief 6.
To prove his case, petitioner examined one witness i.e. himself.

6(i). Petitioner No.1 Vijender Pal @ Bijender Pal (injured) tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A and relied upon following documents :-
 Photocopy of Aadhar Card is Ex. PW1/1
Original referral/ discharge slip is Ex.PW1/2
Original prescriptions, investigation reports are Ex.PW1/3
Original bill of treatment/ medicines are Ex.PW1/4
Original disability certificate is Ex.PW1/5
Copy of criminal case record is Ex.PW1/6
Thereafter, on request of petitioner, PE was closed on 20.03.2023.

Thereafter, on application moved by R3/Sh. Sanjay Aggarwal,
petitioner was allowed to be cross-examined on behalf of R3 and was cross-examined by counsel for R3 on 17.05.2023.
Opportunity of R4 to lead RE was closed on his request.
Opportunity of R1 & R2 to lead RE was also closed as they were absent.
Opportunity of R3 to lead RE was also closed, as R3 failed to lead RE.

7. I have heard Sh. Pankaj Kumar, Ld. counsel for petitioner and Sh. SPS Yadav, Ld. Counsel for R1 & R2 and Sh. S. Ghosh, Ld. counsel for respondent no.4- insurance company and perused the record.
8.
The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1 9.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.

Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
3 10.
Now in this case, the petitioner Vijender @ Bijender Pal is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1 and stated on oath in the affidavit about the accident and how it was caused.
He has clearly deposed that the accident was caused due to vehicle being driven by R1 in a high speed and he being forcibly hit with the vehicle.
Hence, he has stated about the rash and negligent driving of the Respondent No.1, who was the driver of the offending motorcycle.

It is the case of the petitioner as per his testimony that on 26.07.2019 at about 06:30 A.M., when he was going on foot towards Jalebi Chowk and reached just before main road, R1 had come there driving his motorcycle in a zig zag manner from the side of main road at a high speed and hit him.
FIR was registered without delay.
Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle shows accidental impact on the vehicle.
11. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the offending motorcycle.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. In New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648, the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala has held that as a general rule, it can be accepted that production of charge-sheet is prima facie sufficient evidence of negligence for the purpose of claim under section 166 MV Act.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Pazhaniammal (2011) (2) KLT 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any party do not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
13. Respondent No.1/ the driver of the offending vehicle did not led any evidence to prove anything contrary to the claim of the petitioner.

In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.

entities.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the registered owner/R3 and R2/ person stated to be in possession of the offending vehicle and insurance company have not led any evidence to disprove the claim of the petitioner.

MLC of the petitioner shows the nature of injuries as 'grievous'.
14.

In view of above, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities of evidence and for filing of charge-sheet, it is proved that the petitioner Vijender Pal @ Bijender received injuries due to rash and negligent act of Respondent No.1 Manish, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.
ISSUE No.3 15.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
4 16.
The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.

17. Now, in the present case, as per the MLC of petitioner Vijender Pal, he was taken to Lal Bahadur Shashtri Hospital on 26.07.2019 i.e. the date of accident and pain, swelling and internal rotation of right thigh was observed by the doctor.
The nature of the injuries was kept under observation.
The discharge summary of the said hospital dated 27.07.2019 reflects that pre-operation diagnosis was suspected to be the case of fracture and '?? # I/T RT, ?? # proximal femur right' was mentioned.

The medical document of Safdargunj hospital reflects that petitioner visited there on 28.07.2019 with alleged history of road traffic accident and being taken prior to MAX Hospital and brought from thereto Safdarjung Hospital with being a case of pain in right leg.
As per the certificate of Dr. Vivek Aggarwal, which is part of DAR, petitioner was treated in Shanti Mukund Hospital as a case of inter troch fracture right femur and had sustained grievous injury.
The discharge summary dated 21.08.2019 of the petitioner reflects that the history of present illness as reported to the doctor was 'RTA on 26.07.2019 and sustained injury to right hip'.
He was diagnosed with comminuted I/T fracture femur (R).
Petitioner has filed copy of referral summary of MAX Hospital, which reflects that he was taken there on 27.07.2019 i.e. a day after accident with indication and diagnosis of right femur fracture.

On application moved by the petitioner for assessment of disability, he was referred to LBS Hospital and it was reported that he was suffering from 45% physical disability in relation to the right lower limb.
18. From the medical documents on record, it can be safely concluded that petitioner sustained grievous injury in the accident in question.

Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner,
the compensation is awarded to him under the aforesaid heads as follows: -
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
5 19.

entities.text: Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner has proved some of his medical bills.
Under this head, the bills which are on record are of Rs. 2,981/-.

(One of the bills as per the document Ex.PW1/4 dated 18.10.2019 for an amount of Rs.747/- is filed in double and further one of the bills is completely discounted and hence, not calculated in medical expense).
Therefore, I award Rs. 2,981/- as compensation under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
20.
According to his affidavit, after the accident, petitioner was treated in LBS Hospital, MAX Hospital and Shanti Mukund Hospital.
He has deposed in his testimony that after the accident, he was removed to LBS Hospital but only MLC was prepared there and he was discharged.

Thereafter,
he was removed to MAX and admitted thereon 27.07.2019 and discharged on 28.07.2019 due to non-availability of bed with advise to follow-up
and he was referred to other higher centre.
He was thereafter treated at Shanti Mukund Hospital and that his treatment continued for about 04 months.
He deposed that he had sustained several fractures and other injuries.

The MLC of Lal Bahardur Hospital shows that petitioner was taken there on 26.07.2019 with pain and swelling and internal rotation of right thigh and he was referred to Ortho for detailed examination and further investigation and the nature of injuries was kept under observation.

The discharge summary of the said hospital dated 27.07.2019 shows that petitioner underwent operation and was referred for higher centre for the purpose of NCCT-Neuro and asked to follow-up in Ortho OPD.

The document of OPD of Safdarjung Hospital dated 28.07.2019 shows that it was reported to the doctor that after RTA, he was taken to MAX Hospital and brought from thereto Safdarjung Hospital with case of pain in right thigh.
Fracture Right IT femur was observed.
The document of Safdarjung Hospital also shows that he was referred from MAX Hospital to Safdarjung Hospital.

The discharge summary of Shanti Mukund Hospital shows that petitioner was admitted thereon 13.08.2019 and discharged on 21.08.2019 and he was diagnosed with comminuted I/T fracture femur (Right) and history of injury to right hip in the accident was observed.
In view of the above-said discussion, it can be safely concluded that petitioner must have remained under considerable pain for a substantial period of time.
Thus, I find it appropriate to grant a sum of Rs.60,000/- to the petitioner under this head.
CONVEYANCE, SPECIAL DIET & ATTENDANT CHARGES 21.
The petitioner has not proved any actual expenses in relation to these heads and has not placed any material on record to substantiate the said expenses.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it fit to grant Rs.10,000/- to petitioner for conveyance and Rs. 15,000/- for special diet charges.
22. Though petitioner has claimed attendant expenses, no evidence has been led to show that petitioner had hired any attendant during his treatment.

It cannot be ignored that family members of petitioner must have had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner for his routine activities and that would definitely suffer their work/job.

For claiming compensation,
necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
Therefore, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- as attendant charges.

Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
6 23.
Thus, petitioner is granted a total compensation of Rs.45,000/- (10,000+15,000+20,000) under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT AND LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY :
24.

Petitioner has claimed that he was working as Beldar at the time of accident and earning Rs.
16,000/- to Rs.18,000/- per month.
Petitioner claims in his testimony dated 20.03.2023 that he was 65 years old and working as a Beldar at Kalyanpuri, Delhi but not a single document in support of this has been filed on record.

It is relevant to mention that according to the petitioner as disclosed in his cross-examination, he was born in the year 1945 and hence his age at the date of accident dated 26.07.2019 can be considered to be about 74 years old, in absence of any cogent documentary proof of age.
The year of birth as mentioned in the Aadhar Card i.e. '1999' is prima facie false and no other document in proof of age is filed on record.
The treatment paper of the hospital first visited reflects that the age of the petitioner was disclosed in the hospital as 70 years.
There is nothing brought on record to suggest what document, if any, was given in the hospital as identity proof and proof of age.
The Aadhar Card cannot be considered as age proof, particularly in view of the conflicting medical record and testimony of petitioner himself.
The photograph affixed by IO in the memo of parties clearly shows that the petitioner is an old man/an elderly.

Hence, considering that the petitioner was about 74 year old on the date of accident, I am of the view that there should be clear and cogent evidence to show that he was earning on the date of accident and in absence of the same, even the rate of minimum wages cannot be resorted to, to decide on his income and loss of salary/wages.

It is relevant here to mention that this is particularly important, considering that the petitioner had suffered grievous injuries about 05 years back in left lower limb and was operated upon and for reasons best known to the petitioner, he did not disclose it before the Tribunal in his evidence.
There is nothing to suggest that despite sustaining of grievous accident in the year 2014 itself and that too at an advanced age, he could still manage to do labour work as a Beldar.
No employer was examined by the petitioner and no independent witness was examined and even the name and address of employer is not disclosed.
No proof of income is filed either by the petitioner.
It is relevant here to mention that after arguments had been addressed in part, it was observed by the Tribunal, on perusal of the case file,

that in the medical treatment document of Safdarjung hospital,
it was also observed by doctor at Safdarjung Hospital that petitioner had a history of being operated for fracture in lower left limb about 05 years ago at MAX Hospital.

There was nothing to suggest that any document relating to prior accident was produced before the disability board to facilitate in assessment of permanent disability sustained in the accident in question.
Hence, notice was issued to the IO to know about any prior accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.

IO filed on record the discharge summary of MAX Hospital dated 11.01.2014, which shows that the petitioner was admitted there from 08.01.2014 to 11.01.2014 with complaint of pain in left hip following injuries sustained in RTA with initial first aid taken at LBS Hospital.
Neither IO nor petitioner filed on record the treatment document of LBS Hospital dated 08.01.2014 or of any prior period.

On query made by the Tribunal, petitioner filed an affidavit and stated that prior to the accident in question, he had suffered with another accident on 08.01.2015 with an unknown vehicle and the case had been closed by the police and he does not have any documentary proof regarding complaint/statement and treatment record for the accident in the year 2015.

However, no document Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
7 of year 2015 is filed by the petitioner or IO.

entities.text: Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: IO filed on record the certified copy of the discharge summary of the petitioner of MAX Hospital dated 11.01.2024, which reflects that petitioner was presented to the hospital with complaint of pain in left hip following injury sustained in RTA with initial first aid taken at LBS Hospital and presented to emergency with inability to walk and stand.
He was diagnosed with comminuted intertrochanteric fracture left hip with subtrochanteric extension.
An intertrochanteric fracture is a break in the hip that occurs between the greater and lesser trochanters of the femur, the thick bone.
Its the most common type of hip fractures in the elderly (source https.//www. ncbi.nlm.nih.gov and https.//www.orthorbullets.com).

The discharge summary dated 11.01.2014 shows that ORIF left hip fracture with DHS/Plate and interfragmentary fixation for comminuted intertrochanteric fracture with subtrochanteric extension under SA on 09.01.2014 procedures were performed on the petitioner.

It is clear that petitioner has not come before the Tribunal with clean hands by refraining to disclose on his own regarding the prior accident, where he sustained grievous injuries on his left hip with fracture and external rotation deformity of left lower limb.

It was the duty of the petitioner to produce evidence to establish that despite sustaining of such grievous injuries in the year 2015 itself and that too, on the left lower limb with hip involved and with advancing age, he was still capable to work as a Beldar in the year 2019.
No expert evidence has been led to suggest so either.

Though IO has mentioned in the DAR that petitioner is illiterate and 60 years old and worked as a labour, he failed to collect cogent evidence from the petitioner in this regard and did not take into account the previous injury sustained by the petitioner to inquire whether he was actually working and was capable to work.

Petitioner had not filed on record his bank statement to show any earning and no independent witness, including the expert testimony of doctor was got recorded by the petitioner to reflect on his capability to work post accident in the year 2014.

As discussed above, it can be clearly seen that IO did not even bother to ascertain the actual age of the petitioner, which was more than 60 years old even as per the MLC of LBS Hospital, which clearly discloses that the age was mentioned to the Doctor as 70 years.
Even at Safdargunj Hospital, the same age was mentioned.
Interestingly during further visit to Headgewar Hospital, on 05.08.2019, his age was mentioned as 65 years.
In Shanti Mukund Hospital, it is amusing to note that petitioner disclosed his age as 50 years, as per discharge summary dated 21.08.2019.

No document of MAX Hospital is annexed with DAR but petitioner has stated in his testimony that he was treated in MAX Hospital as well pursuant to the accident dt. 26.07.2019 and in the copy of referral summary of MAX Hospital dated 27.07.2019 filed by petitioner, his age is mentioned as 65 years old.
As per the discharge summary of the year 2014 of the petitioner, he was 60 year old at that time only.
Petitioner did not disclose the age and identity related document provided by him and his family in the various hospitals and apparently the age on the Aadhar Card is false.

Suggestions were given to PW1/Petitioner by Ld. Counsel for R4/Insurer that he was not working as a Beldar and not earning at the time of accident and has not suffered any functional disability on account of injuries sustained in the accident in question.

Though, these suggestions were denied by the petitioner, no such fitness certificate or medical document post 11.01.2014 has been filed and proved on record to establish that petitioner was capable to work as a Beldar at the age of 74 years, despite sustaining of such serious injuries in the year 2014 itself and hence, in absence of any work and income proof, the loss of wages/income and functional disability of the petitioner has to be taken as Nil.
Hence, no amount is being given as compensation under this head.

8 25.

Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-
 Sl. No.
Head of compensation Amount

1 Medical Expenses Rs.2,981/-
 2 Pain & Suffering Rs.60,000/-
 3 Conveyance & Special diet Rs.25,000/-
 4 Attendant charges Rs.20,000/-
 Loss of income during Nil  treatment and loss of future  income on account of  permanent disability  TOTAL Rs.1,07,981/-
 (Round off to Rs.
 1,08,000/-)
INTEREST 25.
Petitioner has pursued his case since the year 2019.

Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5%
per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

LIABILITY:
27.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.

The insurance company has not examined any witness to prove the objections raised by it and to prove that term or condition of insurance policy was breached/
violated by insured as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.

However, it is seen that as per the charge-sheet itself, the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. R1 did not have a driving licence on the date of accident and offence under Section 3/181 was also mentioned/added in the charge-sheet.
R1 to R3 did not lead any evidence to suggest that R1 was having a valid driving licence on the date of accident.

The statement of R1 was recorded by Ld. Predecessor of the Tribunal under Order X CPC on 12.02.2020,
where he stated on oath that he was driving the offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing Registration No.DL-4SCF-6004 at the time of accident.

Hence, even though,
no evidence was led by the insurance company to prove the breach in question, it is apparent that R1 did not have driving licence and hence, there was breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

The copy of the insurance policy is part of DAR and shows that therein, it is stipulated that the person entitled to drive was any person including insured, provided he holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident.

Hence, the breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
9 hitting at the route of the contract of insurance is established.

entities.text: Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the breach in question is not such as would affect the right of third party, once it is established that vehicle was covered under the policy of insurance.
Law is well settled that insurance company would be entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the driver and registered owner /insured of the offending vehicle.

In case titled as Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023, it has been held that the insurer is entitled to recover the compensation amount paid to the claimants.

entities.text: Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In such circumstances, insurance company is entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the respondent No.1 i.e. driver and Respondent No.3/registered owner of offending vehicle, jointly and severally, after paying the aforesaid compensation to the petitioner in the first place.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.4/ insurer shall be entitled to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

RELIEF:
28.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.1,08,000/- (Rs. One Lakh Eight Thousand only)
along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.4/
United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
If any party do not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
In the case of Cholamandalam MS General Insurance Cmpany Ltd vs Smt. Kamlesh and Others2009 (3) AD Delhi 310 it was held that an adverse inference can be drawn when the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter into the witness box.
The compensation should not be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not resulting loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities in consequent to his injuries.
For claiming compensation,
necessity of employing a professional attendant/ care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
The year of birth as mentioned in the Aadhar Card i.e. '1999' is prima facie false and no other document in proof of age is filed on record.
There is nothing brought on record to suggest what document, if any, was given in the hospital as identity proof and proof of age.
The Aadhar Card cannot be considered as age proof, particularly in view of the conflicting medical record and testimony of petitioner himself.
Hence, considering that the petitioner was about 74 year old on the date of accident, I am of the view that there should be clear and cogent evidence to show that he was earning on the date of accident and in absence of the same, even the rate of minimum wages cannot be resorted to, to decide on his income and loss of salary/wages.
Hence, no amount is being given as compensation under this head.
R1 to R3 did not lead any evidence to suggest that R1 was having a valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The statement of R1 was recorded by Ld. Predecessor of the Tribunal under Order X CPC on 12.02.2020,
where he stated on oath that he was driving the offending vehicle i.e. motorcycle bearing Registration No.DL-4SCF-6004 at the time of accident.
Hence, even though,
no evidence was led by the insurance company to prove the breach in question, it is apparent that R1 did not have driving licence and hence, there was breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The copy of the insurance policy is part of DAR and shows that therein, it is stipulated that the person entitled to drive was any person including insured, provided he holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Hence, the breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as Vijender @ Bijender Pal vs Manish on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105787221/
9 hitting at the route of the contract of insurance is established.
However, the breach in question is not such as would affect the right of third party, once it is established that vehicle was covered under the policy of insurance.
Law is well settled that insurance company would be entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the driver and registered owner /insured of the offending vehicle.
In case titled as Gurmeet Singh vs. The New India Assurance Co. Ltd & Ors, MAC App 288/2021 decided on 06.10.2023, it has been held that the insurer is entitled to recover the compensation amount paid to the claimants.

In such circumstances, insurance company is entitled for recovery of the compensation amount from the respondent No.1 i.e. driver and Respondent No.3/registered owner of offending vehicle, jointly and severally, after paying the aforesaid compensation to the petitioner in the first place.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.4/ insurer shall be entitled to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.
